Frequently Asked Questions

What is Attekmi?
Everything started with SmartHub, an ad exchange solution that revolutionized the AdTech industry. To keep up pace with the market and meet the needs of a wider audience, we extended our offer and decided to rebrand to mark this stage of our growth. This is how Attekmi, a brand offering multiple AdTech products and services, entered the stage.
What kind of businesses can benefit from Attekmi products and services?
Our ad exchange solutions are mainly in demand among media agencies, ad networks, and AdTech & media startups that are willing to start earning on media trading quickly. Additionally, any business operating in the AdTech industry (or going to do so) can benefit from our custom development and AdOps training services.
Is it secure to use Attekmi products?
Ad fraud has always been a problem for all the participants of the AdTech industry. That is why we provide you with an opportunity to integrate demand and supply scanners into your Attekmi solutions. This way, you can fraud-proof the system and keep your marketplace secure.
Does Attekmi offer a free consultation?
There is no need to pay to learn more about our products or services. Just get in touch with us, and we will be glad to answer all your questions.
What are white label AdTech solutions?
A white label advertising platform refers to a product that you purchase from another company and rebrand it as your own. However, in the case of our White Label AdEx, you get even more than rebranding – the platform gets tailored specifically to your needs, so feel free to request custom features that will make your white label programmatic advertising company stand out in the market.

CVE-2023-44487.summary: The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.

CVE-2021-3618.summary: ALPACA is an application layer protocol content confusion attack, exploiting TLS servers implementing different protocols but using compatible certificates, such as multi-domain or wildcard certificates. A MiTM attacker having access to victim's traffic at the TCP/IP layer can redirect traffic from one subdomain to another, resulting in a valid TLS session. This breaks the authentication of TLS and cross-protocol attacks may be possible where the behavior of one protocol service may compromise the other at the application layer.

CVE-2021-23017.summary: A security issue in nginx resolver was identified, which might allow an attacker who is able to forge UDP packets from the DNS server to cause 1-byte memory overwrite, resulting in worker process crash or potential other impact.

CVE-2025-23419.summary:
When multiple server blocks are configured to share the same IP address and port, an attacker can use session resumption to bypass client certificate authentication requirements on these servers. This vulnerability arises when  TLS Session Tickets https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssl_module.html#ssl_session_ticket_key  are used and/or the  SSL session cache https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_ssl_module.html#ssl_session_cache  are used in the default server and the default server is performing client certificate authentication.  

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.
